obligations.title: field-wise Scope merge
obligations.evidence: auth_merge_kind, option_child_wins/option_child_presence, options_apply and append_vec are mechanized/used; append-only container/list fields merge through the verified helper; environment_origin_merge_preserves_tags models every environment value and its main/access origin as one tuple, matching runtime Originated<T>, so append cannot detach or upgrade provenance. Resolved-target restriction now merges tagged environment and content policy with the URL identity last, retaining both identities' remove/unset lists. Header set uses ordered child replacement audited by the debug container snapshot; ErrorDocument and RewriteMap are list-backed with reverse child-wins lookup; parser and Options-list construction remain outside this obligation

obligations.title: Directory < Files < Location < Condition
obligations.evidence: config_rule_phase, config_deferred_slot and config_rule_precedes are executable specifications consumed through an exhaustive MatchKind projection by phase collection and the recursive nested-rule sorter; config_rule_order_is_asymmetric proves the comparator cannot order a pair both ways. access_plan_interleaves proves the exact source/depth plan consumed by the runtime: DirectoryConfig then optional DirectoryAccess at each root-to-leaf depth, Directory own-path and DirectoryMatch, BaseFiles, FilesConfig then optional FilesAccess at each depth, DirectoryMatch Files, Location, config conditions and access conditions. condition_source_plan_exec is consumed by request_plan when it applies config conditions before access-file conditions, and its proof ties that order to the access-plan tail. Access-file IfFile is evaluated while parsing against an absolute ServerRoot path and its children retain their native Directory/Files phases; iffile_exec_on_read_admit is consumed at that splice. Standard-library sort correctness and parser directive/pattern payload semantics remain outside Verus.

obligations.title: per-directory Directory; access-file interleaving
obligations.evidence: AccessStep names config versus access-file provenance and exact depth for both Directory and Files phases; access_plan_exec is the only production iteration plan, and access_plan_interleaves proves its structural equality and suffix. The access walk covers every ancestor whose effective AllowOverride permits a layer and is not bounded by DocumentRoot or an alias target (access_walk_dir_admit, I47). AccessLayer parsing and filesystem discovery remain refinement assumptions.

obligations.title: Require/PolicyResult semantics
obligations.evidence: PolicyResult combinators and require_none are verified; expression integer/string comparison and glob matching run through verified kernels (expr_compare_ints, expr_compare_strs, expr_glob_match). P15 expression regexes compile as PCRE2 at configuration load, and expr_regex_result proves an evaluation error cannot grant even through negation; provider/auth backends and PCRE2's internal matching semantics remain outside the model.

obligations.title: RequireNone cannot grant
obligations.evidence: require_none_result proved and consumed by access.rs

obligations.title: AllowOverride/AllowOverrideList/Nonfatal gate
obligations.evidence: override_mode_allows is the executable category-bit admission kernel used by OverrideMode::allows/allows_flag; htaccess_section_category_admit and htaccess_section_admit totalize every supported section command and independently gate it by its Apache category mask or exact AllowOverrideList '<Section' entry, so a listed child cannot admit an unlisted top-level wrapper. htaccess_section_nonfatal_override_admit pins Apache's fail-closed execute-on-read section subset; nested authz containers are admitted only after their outer authz command has passed while child directives remain gated. htaccess_gate_admit is the single final apply/skip/reject disposition before the effectful parser. The exhaustive parser matrix and 96 paired Apache wrapper cases cover child-only/exact lists, category masks and Nonfatal behavior.

obligations.title: htaccess/cache prefilter over-approximation
obligations.evidence: prefilter_sound proves both boolean implications in Verus: htaccess_may_apply false admits no access-file layer, and a false cache prefilter over an unchanged base enable list keeps cache_enabled false; the path-pattern matcher, recursive rule flattening and parser-to-ActiveLayer refinement remain explicit assumptions

obligations.title: ACL reachability and resource binding
obligations.evidence: I1a exact ResourceKey grants and I1b inode/backend/policy binding feed the executable TransformCapability state. Every protected file, directory, CGI, FastCGI, proxy, WebSocket and cache sink calls AccessGrant::require_sink, which combines exact resource equality with the verified sink-specific admission predicate. I31 opens and reauthorizes CGI and FastCGI scripts before binding the selected inode; P15 FastCGI binds transport, lexical SCRIPT_FILENAME, authorized canonical path and PATH_INFO, with fastcgi_script_identity_admit proving that neither script identity can be omitted. P17 adds fastcgi_resolved_target_admit at the SetHandler constructor so its lexical classification/wire path cannot be replaced by the canonical authorization path. P18-B2 rebuilds a configuration-only scope for every selected ProxyPass/ProxyPassMatch or FastCGI route and consumes proxy_operator_acl_admit before the access-file-restricted scope, so access files may narrow but never supply the operator grant. Authorization providers and request-plan refinement remain outside this obligation.

obligations.title: Ordered competing request-to-resource mappings
obligations.evidence: first_match_is_first and first_match_none_means_no_match prove that the selected match bit is the first true one and that no bit means no match, so a later overlapping route cannot win; Alias/AliasMatch/ScriptAliasMatch and Redirect/RedirectMatch use this order, ProxyPass/ProxyPassMatch share one route_order space, handler operations use last-match wins, and unit/differential tests cover order reversal; flattening the runtime tables to the match-bit vector remains outside Verus

obligations.title: Every target-changing transform reauthorizes the sink
obligations.evidence: TransformCapability is an executable Verus state machine: retarget clears authorization and every binding, authorize binds the current target, and inode/backend transitions add only their exact capability. transform_retarget_requires_reauthorization proves a retargeted state cannot reach any sink; transform_sink_implies_reauthorized plus the file/backend/cache lemmas prove every admitted sink has the required bindings. AccessGrant::require_sink is the runtime projection at every protected sink, and exact ResourceKey equality makes a pre-transform grant unusable after a target change. The I30 inventory covers alias, CGI/FastCGI PATH_INFO and handlers, symlinks, rewrites, DirectoryIndex, ErrorDocument, DirectorySlash, proxy/balancer failover, cache targets and WebSocket.

obligations.title: Scheme, peer, canonical name and identity have trusted sources
obligations.evidence: HTTPS/REQUEST_SCHEME come from listener TLS state, UseCanonicalName uses ServerName, and identity comes from verified authenticators. RemoteIP retains Apache's internal/trusted proxy classes; remoteip_next_internal and remoteip_candidate_admit mechanize the one-way class transition and rejection of private values presented by an external chain. The parser/walk projection and broader context-construction refinement remain partial.

obligations.title: Untrusted streams have bounded size and deadlines
obligations.evidence: I33 covers request/proxy trailer count and byte budgets, proxy chunk checked_add before resize, CGI worker path/env/body/output caps, FastCGI record/header/stdout/stderr caps, HTTP/2 budgets and compression. resource_budget_admit mechanizes overflow-free aggregate admission; RAII runtime leases enforce shared spool-byte/file, request/response resident-byte, blocking-read, HTTP/2-stream and CGI/FastCGI concurrency ceilings across reloads. P20 makes both HTTP adapters consume one incremental BodyAccumulator and request_body_memory_admit proves each resident-prefix extension is bounded. Follow-up gates prove successful-only cache invalidation, autoindex scan/render arithmetic, bcrypt cost and PCRE2 input bounds; runtime limits proxy and CGI responses, DNS workers, expensive CPU work and byte-counted policy/auth/access caches. Body/header parsing uses hard deadlines, HTTP/2 is capped at 32 streams per connection and 256 process-wide, and connection spawn/descriptor exhaustion paths are regression-tested. Request-time expression file reads consume expr_file_read_admit, reject non-regular descriptors, use O_NONBLOCK/O_NOFOLLOW and read at most 64 KiB. Kernel/socket scheduling and upstream protocol implementations remain outside the model.

obligations.title: Header set/add/unset/always semantics across all response paths
obligations.evidence: Static, directory, redirect, CGI/FastCGI, proxy and error responses apply the ordered header policy; child set replaces, unset runs last, always applies to errors; merge/application proofs are unit-tested but not mechanized

obligations.title: Every positive terminal outcome enforces original-URL and current-target grants
obligations.evidence: TransformCapability plus AccessGrant::require_sink mechanize the final exact-resource and sink-binding gate for static/directory, CGI/FastCGI, proxy, WebSocket and cache outcomes. Original-URL and current-target scopes are both enforced and F23 covers rewrite-then-proxy/redirect. Redirect and error-response orchestration remain runtime projections outside the protected body/tunnel/cache sink state machine, so the broader all-positive-outcomes obligation remains partial.

obligations.title: Reload advances a cache generation and stale entries are never served
obligations.evidence: cache_lookup_admit binds key/policy/Vary/generation/freshness; cache_lookup_hit_requires_binding and cache_lookup_rejects_stale mechanize the consequences; disk metadata records the epoch, reload clears memory/disk and bumps the epoch, and PATH_INFO keys resolve to the actual CGI script; expiry uses verified saturating cache_expiry so positive TTLs cannot wrap into the past; admission is verified, reload orchestration is not

obligations.title: map_path, access-file walk and cache consume one alias-root identity
obligations.evidence: Relative AliasMatch/ScriptAliasMatch roots are resolved against ServerRoot at compile time and access_root_for uses the same alias table; absolute/prefix and relative/capture-only forms are unit-tested

obligations.title: Autoindex and generated headers use sink-context encoders
obligations.evidence: safe_relative_href prefixes './' before URL encoding so hostile names cannot become javascript:/data:/scheme-relative links; header values pass the verified sanitizer that now rejects every control byte except HTAB plus DEL

obligations.title: Require providers consume exactly the post-not operand
obligations.evidence: parse_require uses rest.first() for env and rest.join(' ') for expr; the verified require_env_operand_admit rejects empty or NAME=VALUE operands, require_method_operand_admit accepts only exact supported method tokens, and expression variables are load-time validated; Require::Expr and Require::ValidUser both carry negation; unit and HTTP-level tests cover the provider and negation shapes

obligations.title: Every accepted .htaccess directive is modeled, explicitly inert, or rejected
obligations.evidence: htaccess SetEnv/SetEnvIf/UnsetEnv/PassEnv and IndexIgnore populate EnvironmentPolicy/ContentPolicy through the same parser as main config; RequestHeader is rejected instead of accepted as inert; DIRECTIVE_SPECS is the authoritative disposition/category registry and an exhaustive test matrix asserts every entry is effectful, inert or rejected and is gated by AllowOverride None; I34 adds the main-config fail-closed matrix for security, filter, audit and resource-limit directives plus explicit compatibility-inert warnings

obligations.title: Autoindex policy and /dir versus /dir/ authorization
obligations.evidence: IndexIgnore filters listing entries in main config and .htaccess; DirectorySlash Off reauthorizes a no-slash directory target as the canonical trailing-slash URL before index/listing dispatch

obligations.title: Regex alias targets remain inside their configured alias base
obligations.evidence: map_path returns an explicit mapping failure when a capture-only or absolute AliasMatch/ScriptAliasMatch expansion leaves fs_path; the parent-root fallback is removed; alias admission now consumes the verified component-aware path_under_base kernel (including the /srv/www versus /srv/www2 boundary), and unit plus end-to-end F31 cases cover the escape shape

obligations.title: Internal rewrite filesystem targets never change the authorization base
obligations.evidence: verified rewrite_filesystem_shape_admit rejects external, passthrough and relative substitutions before filesystem lookup; rewrite_filesystem_candidate_admit composes that shape gate with the existing is-file and component-aware path_under_base containment checks. The runtime consumes both verified gates directly, UnsafePrefixStat cannot re-root at the target parent, and rewrite-condition file tests probe the canonicalized target path rather than its lexical spelling. The rewrite target scope remains conjoined with both rewritten and original URL policy.

obligations.title: FastCGI script and PATH_INFO targets are bounded by the configured base
obligations.evidence: script_from_prefix and split_path_info clean/canonicalize the script inside the FastCGI prefix or document/alias root and consume the verified component-aware path_under_base kernel; the ancestor walk cannot select an ancestor file such as /bin/sh or a sibling with a shared byte prefix such as www2; unit cases cover dot segments, $1 templates, sibling-prefix targets and outside targets

obligations.title: Cache keys bind request inputs that select authorization branches
obligations.evidence: cache_policy_material destructures Scope and hashes every policy slice (rewrite maps canonicalized); cache_policy_fingerprint frames each exact field with the verified injective cache_fingerprint_field and uses a 256-bit SHA-256 digest instead of the old 64-bit DefaultHasher; the digest also binds all request headers, peer, method and target. V4 disk metadata stores the complete base key, lookup consumes cache_disk_key_admit for an exact metadata-key match, and canonical unsafe-method invalidation consumes cache_invalidation_remove_admit so unrelated keyed entries survive. The unit matrix mutates every policy field plus listener/vhost/URL/query/target/header dimensions, and F34 replay verifies header partitioning

obligations.title: Upstream request lines and forwarded headers reject control injection
obligations.evidence: backend authorities are validated at parse time; RewriteRule [P] templates consume rewrite_template_static so every runtime capture/variable spelling ($N, %N, \N, ${...}, %{...}) is rejected from the authority; X-Forwarded-Host is checked before insertion. HTTP and WebSocket request construction, final-head validation, upstream write, response-line parsing and Location rewriting operate on bytes; validate_proxy_head applies proxy_request_line_admit and proxy_header_admit immediately before every upstream write, and raw-query/obs-text integration tests prove byte preservation

obligations.title: Authenticated identity reaches CGI and FastCGI environment
obligations.evidence: the access-grant identity is carried into CgiContext and build_env emits REMOTE_USER/AUTH_TYPE for local CGI and FastCGI; configured environment entries remain unable to override reserved names; unit and F38 replay cases cover Basic auth

obligations.title: Single-file aliases map to parent plus basename
obligations.evidence: prefix Alias/ScriptAlias file targets are split into parent plus basename, the access-file walk uses the parent, and handler/MIME/FastCGI selection consumes the resolved basename; alias_file_target_split, alias_access_root_admit and handler_name_from_target are mechanized and the F39 replay covers .htaccess deny plus CGI source disclosure

obligations.title: Effectful directives inside <Limit> are applied or rejected
obligations.evidence: main-configuration Options/Header/AddHandler/SetHandler inside <Limit> are applied to the enclosing scope instead of warn-and-ignored, while auth/access directives remain method-scoped; .htaccess rejects non-auth directives; limit_directive_effect is mechanized and config/unit plus F40 replay cases cover Options -ExecCGI and -Indexes

obligations.title: CGI/FastCGI reauthorize and bind the actual target
obligations.evidence: the dispatcher binds the opened target before handler selection; PATH_INFO reauthorizes fd_path(file). FastCGI now resolves the script through an open descriptor, reauthorizes its actual fd path, binds both dev/inode and the exact backend identity, and reopens plus compares dev/inode immediately before emitting SCRIPT_FILENAME. cgi_actual_target_admit is mechanized and the F41 replay covers direct, PATH_INFO and FastCGI symlink targets. Pass-11 classification (is_cgi) is a single cgi_exec_admit kernel call with fail-closed lemmas, evaluated on the lexical basename while containment stays on the resolved target.

obligations.title: Capture-only regex aliases have no implicit ServerRoot base
obligations.evidence: Alias::regex keeps an empty base for leading-capture replacements and map_path fails closed for every empty-base mapping; capture_only_alias_admit is mechanized and the F42 replay asserts .htpasswd, rewrite secrets and the configuration are not readable

obligations.title: Spool/temp files use exclusive creation and private mode
obligations.evidence: the FastCGI spool uses create_new, mode 0600, bounded collision retries and immediate unlink; temp_file_create_admit is mechanized and unit cases plant a symlink at the predicted name and verify the target is untouched and the descriptor is private

obligations.title: Disk and resident cache tiers have independent byte quotas
obligations.evidence: cache_disk_projected and cache_disk_evict mechanize replacement projection and monotone eviction; persisted bytes are tracked per cache root, CacheMaxDiskSize and MAX_DISK_ENTRIES are enforced by evicting the oldest stems, oversized entries are refused, expired/old-generation files are deleted on load, per-key variants are capped, and CacheIgnoreQueryString bypasses dynamic CGI/FastCGI/proxy targets. The independent CacheMaxMemorySize counter includes key, body, response headers and Vary material; cache_memory_admit bounds overflow-free insertion and replacement, oldest entries are evicted under the lock, bodies above 64 KiB remain disk-only, and lookup clones an Arc rather than copying a retained body under the process-wide mutex

obligations.title: Expression file tests use the document-root confinement
obligations.evidence: Expr::FileTest consumes confined_expr_path for -f/-d/-e/-s/-F/-U, rejecting absolute, parent-relative and escaping-symlink arguments; the containment check consumes the verified component-aware path_under_base kernel. Config compilation binds the effective default or explicit DocumentRoot into every global/vhost scope, and synthetic empty-root scopes fail closed rather than falling back to '/'. Main-config <IfFile> uses a separate operator-supplied Expr::IfFile; unit and P14 regressions cover absent-DocumentRoot, absolute, parent-relative and escaping-symlink cases; rewrite condition file tests also canonicalize and consume path_under_base.

obligations.title: RequireNone fails when any child provider is satisfied
obligations.evidence: combine_or_all and require_none_multi aggregate every child as an OR of positive hits before negation, so a granted child cannot be neutralized by a denied sibling; access.rs consumes require_none_multi and require_none_multi_result is the mechanized disposition predicate; main-config, .htaccess, unit and generated Apache differential cases cover two-provider and three-provider block lists

obligations.title: Regex alias file targets use parent plus basename and the parent access root
obligations.evidence: map_path splits a regex alias target that resolves to a regular file into parent plus basename with or without a trailing slash in the replacement; the URL/base root uses the file parent via alias_access_root_admit for regex and prefix aliases alike, while ancestor authorization follows I47 independently of that root; unit plus F47 replays cover AliasMatch/ScriptAliasMatch static and CGI targets

obligations.title: Virtual-host selection is bound to destination address and port
obligations.evidence: Config::select_vhost consumes vhost_address_admit and vhost_address_precedence with the destination address; address-bound vhosts are ineligible on another address and exact-address vhosts precede wildcard vhosts; HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, WebSocket, cache and logging pass the local address, TLS filters vhosts when the listener has a concrete address, and unit plus F48 replays cover both loopback addresses

obligations.title: Authorization consumes a canonical IPv4/IPv6 peer identity
obligations.evidence: ipv4_mapped_to_v4 is the verified conversion consumed by access::canonical_ip; the accept boundary and RemoteIP path canonicalize before request context construction, and ip_in_net, Require local, logs, cache and CGI identities use the canonical peer; unit plus dual-stack F49 replays cover mapped deny, allow and local cases

obligations.title: Access-file walk covers every applicable ancestor
obligations.evidence: access_walk_dir_admit states that each ancestor participates when its effective AllowOverride policy permits a layer; collect_layers/apply_req_deferred walk filesystem ancestors without a DocumentRoot or alias-root lower bound, and access_file_layer_read no longer contains an under_root conjunct; unit plus F50 replays cover DocumentRoot parent Basic auth/deny, directory index, CGI, cache lookup and alias-target parents; lexical and canonical AllowOverride identities are conjoined so an explicit None on either path denies the canonical access file (F60-D)

obligations.title: Mapping root comes from URL-selected alias
obligations.evidence: alias_mapping_root_admit states that a root inferred from alias-target containment is never admitted; map_path returns the URL-selected root and dispatch, cache, rewrite reauthorization and --explain pass it to the access walk for RewriteBase/URL-base derivation only; unit plus F51 replays cover overlapping prefix/regex Alias, ScriptAlias and both alias orders

obligations.title: DirectoryIndex cache key and policy bind the selected target
obligations.evidence: cache_directory_index_bind_admit requires an index-selected directory cache entry to bind both key and policy to the index; cache_ignore_query_admit forbids merging dynamic index/script representations across queries; request_scope resolves DirectoryIndex, re-evaluates the index scope and binds the opened index target before lookup/store; unit plus F52 replays cover cross-query CGI indexes and live <Files> denies for directory and direct index URLs

obligations.title: Canonical REQUEST_URI for expressions, rewrites and environment rules
obligations.evidence: request_uri_identity_admit requires REQUEST_URI to be bound to the dispatcher's canonical URL path, query-free and never the raw request-line target. RequestPlan supplies that target to dispatch, cache and --explain; expr::Context::new, Scope::request_env, access::check, rewrite::Context::for_plan and CGI build_env consume the canonical URL path. Require expr/<If>, SetEnvIf Request_URI, RewriteCond and substitution expansion no longer read req.target or append the query string. Unit plus F57 raw-socket replays cover query suffixes, percent-encoded names, dot segments, allow-list and deny-list shapes

obligations.title: One immutable request plan for dispatch, cache, rewrite and explain
obligations.evidence: RequestPlan is built once per request or rewrite round from CanonicalTarget and map_path, collects the access-file layers once, and exposes canonical URL path, mapping root, relative/fs paths, script-alias state and layers. dispatch_inner_request passes the same plan to cache lookup/store and dispatch; cache no longer re-decodes raw_path or rebuilds mapping; rewrite::Context::for_plan consumes plan identity; --explain prints the plan's canonical path, mapping, layer directories, URL mounts and subjects. Explicit-target plans walk the supplied fs_path itself (never root.join(file_name)), inherit AllowOverride policy from the lexically mapped directory when the root is a symlink, always consume a nonempty layer set, and fail closed when a layer does not belong to the target (explicit_target_layer_admit and target_layer_consume_admit, I60). text_identity_admit rejects non-UTF-8 root, relative and resolved filesystem identities before layer collection, and config/access/MIME parsers reject invalid UTF-8 bytes. Integration coverage exercises cache hits, rewrite rounds, CGI PATH_INFO, DirectoryIndex, explain and the F59 symlinked-root regressions; the universal refinement theorem remains open; pass-10 I61 conjoins the URL-mapped and canonical/rewrite target scopes instead of replacing the lexical scope

obligations.title: Resolved-target scope is a meet with the URL-mapped scope
obligations.evidence: options_conjoin computes the bitwise meet of URL and canonical target Options; handler_conjoin_admit permits an extension only when both identities resolve to the same handler, and conjoined_handlers projects disagreement to RemoveHandler; override_categories_conjoin plus OverridePolicy::conjoined_with make an explicit AllowOverride None on either path identity deny the canonical access file. Scope::restrict_with is consumed by symlink target binding, DirectorySlash/PATH_INFO/FastCGI target reauthorization, rewrite filesystem targets and cache script/index/canonical targets (F60/I61). Content and tagged environment policy are retained from both identities with the URL identity applied last; remove/unset entries from either survive. The Options and AllowOverride-category meets share bits_meet with no-broadening and algebraic lemmas. Unit, htaccess policy, two symlink Apache differentials and F60 end-to-end cases cover handlers, content, environment, -Indexes and AllowOverride denial; SetHandler force conjoins through set_handler_conjoin_admit.

obligations.title: One verified percent-encoding loop for every escape site
obligations.evidence: percent_encode refines to percent_encode_from with out@ equality, a 3x length bound, identity on unmasked input (percent_encode_from_identity) and no-raw-masked-byte output (no_masked_raw/percent_encode_no_masked_raw, given an alphabet-safe mask). Rewrite backreference [B]/[BNE]/[BCTLS]/[BNP] escaping, redirect-Location escaping (which now also escapes non-ASCII bytes instead of emitting Latin-1 mojibake) and the int:escape map all consume the one verified loop; the per-site masks remain runtime data outside Verus and int:unescape remains unverified

obligations.title: Component-aware containment composes across path identities
obligations.evidence: path_under_base_reflexive and path_under_base_transitive mechanize composition of the verified component-aware containment kernel: every base contains itself, and target-under-mid plus mid-under-base implies target-under-base for the lexical byte domain. expr file-test confinement consumes path_under_base. Protected filesystem sinks resolve with mandatory openat2/descriptor binding and FastCGI plus access-file parsing validate descriptor snapshots; configuration testing and startup fail closed when the syscall or required resolution flags are unavailable, with no canonicalize/open fallback. Parser-to-path construction remains a refinement boundary. The endpoint-keyed VapacheFastCGIStablePath projection is required by default, denies unregistered backends, checks Unix socket owner/inode stability, rejects POSIX ACLs and checks lexical/canonical component ownership and mode against the configured worker UID; only the explicit UnstableFastCgiPaths capability retains the equivalent read-only-tree proof-debt assumption.

obligations.title: Expression parsing is total: malformed input errors, never panics
obligations.evidence: Implemented; agent handoff item H1. Parser::regex() bounds-checks that a delimiter byte exists after =~/!~ and fails closed with an error instead of panicking ('expected a regex after =~'); the recursive-descent parser gained a depth budget (MAX_EXPR_DEPTH 64 for the primary/unary frames, chosen so the worst ~2 KiB-per-level chain stay under the 2 MiB default thread stacks used by request handlers) enforced in wrapper functions that decrement on every return path; a depth overflow returns Err rather than aborting. Unit tests cover the end-of-operator panic shape and depth exhaustion (expr.rs tests in cargo test -p vapached).

obligations.title: Rewrite flags and rounds select one target: [PT] maps URLs, overrides are not sticky, dead flags warn
obligations.evidence: Partially implemented. rewrite_expand_token is the shared executable alphabet for variable/rule-capture/condition-capture interpretation and proxy-template admission. rewrite_match_action is the single post-match decision for chain failure, [F], [G], '-' and expansion; rewrite_advance is the shared bounded program-counter transition for [S], [N], [L] and [END] after both '-' and internal substitutions. rewrite_unmatched_rule_has_no_terminal_effect and rewrite_restart_cannot_fall_through prove the key control exclusions, while rewrite_chain_resume proves failed-chain skipping. rewrite_sink, rewrite_query_action and filesystem shape/candidate kernels cover terminal sink, query and [PT] selection. Runtime truth-table and dash-[END] regressions consume these executable forms. Regex matching, variable values, filesystem observations and target-string construction remain outside Verus.

obligations.title: Signless Options words reset the set like Apache
obligations.evidence: Implemented; agent handoff item H3. Both parsers (config.rs main-config Options arm and htaccess.rs apply_options) now collect recognized signless words into a reset mask and apply push_set(Options::empty()) followed by the mask and the compiled FollowSymLinks default BEFORE the per-word loop, so `Options Indexes` resets the inheritance set exactly as the Apache oracle does: inherited ExecCGI is dropped and the compiled default bits return. Differential coverage agrees on both engines (htaccess-options-absolute-resets-inherited, htaccess-options-none-removes-indexes in tests/config_semantics.py); +/- sign and per-word semantics are unchanged. The runtime options_apply transition now has proofs that Set replaces the parent, Add preserves every existing bit while adding the mask, and Remove cannot grant bits and clears the requested mask.

obligations.title: RewriteMap sources are validated and bounded at load time
obligations.evidence: txt/rnd map loads fail closed when missing, unreadable, invalid UTF-8 or larger than MAX_REWRITEMAP; int maps reject unknown functions. prg helpers resolve against ServerRoot, must be executable regular files no larger than 64 MiB, and are copied from one descriptor snapshot into a sealed memfd. Each lookup reopens the configured pathname only to verify the original dev/inode/version, then executes the immutable descriptor with a process-group deadline and 8 KiB output cap. Rename replacement, same-inode mutation, non-file/oversized helpers, sealing and shebang execution are regression-tested; descriptor_snapshot_admit is the executable identity/version gate.

obligations.title: [CO=...] cookie fields parse under a strict grammar
obligations.evidence: Implemented; agent handoff item H5. build_cookie validates the RFC 6265 grammar before emitting: the cookie name must be an RFC 6265 token, value/Domain/Path must be field-octets (ASCII graphic plus space; ';', ',', '"' and DEL/controls rejected), SameSite only accepts lax|strict|none (case-insensitive) and secure/httponly only their true|1|secure|httponly tokens, so a backref containing ':' or ';' can no longer shift fields or inject attributes and fails closed with Err. The old tolerant '0'/'false' flag spellings were removed and the matching suite expectation was updated to the strict spelling; the compiled flag-file conformance case [CO=TEST:VAL:localhost:3600:/:secure:httponly:none] still conforms. Unit tests: cookie_escape_and_effect_helpers in rewrite.rs.

obligations.title: Raw query bytes reach authorization without lossy conflation
obligations.evidence: ResourceKey.cache_query is Option<Vec<u8>> so raw query strings keep byte identity in cache keys. %{QUERY_STRING} expression evaluation and the rewrite variable fail closed when text is required. At byte-string protocol boundaries, HTTP/WebSocket proxy request lines and CGI QUERY_STRING now preserve every raw query byte instead of using lossy UTF-8; integration/unit tests cover 0xff queries and obs-text headers. The deliberate fail-closed expression/rewrite divergence from Apache remains flagged for review.

obligations.title: .htaccess <IfFile> tests the operator-supplied path
obligations.evidence: Implemented; agent handoff item H7. The .htaccess <IfFile> arm now tests the operator-supplied argument (SectionStart.args excludes the tag, mirroring the main-config args.first() use), so single-argument <IfFile flag> tests the named file rather than the empty path that forced the section on; a two-word <IfFile a b> tests 'a' and documents the second word as ignored. Apache (local 2.4.69) resolves .htaccess <IfFile> relative paths against ServerRoot while vapached confines .htaccess file probes to relative DocumentRoot paths (F45/I42, CVE-2026-24072/44119), so the differential suite cases were reshaped to relative paths that exist under both roots (tests/config_semantics.py htaccess-*-iffile*, plus the new negative branch htaccess-all-iffile-absent); absolute-path .htaccess <IfFile> stays FALSE (a deliberate fail-closed divergence under the user-approved parity waiver). Unit test: htaccess.rs iffile_tests_the_operator_path_not_a_second_word.

obligations.title: Strict configuration rejects every silently dropped directive
obligations.evidence: Implemented; agent handoff item H8. New Compile::strict_failure helper: under --strict-config a silent drop becomes a ConfigError, in compatible mode it logs 'file:line: msg (ignored)'. Promoted: under-argument AddType/AddHandler, Header (action requires an argument pair), ExpiresByType (type + code), ProxyPass (path + backend), unknown Options tokens, unknown RewriteOptions tokens, and unparsable failonstatus entries for ProxyPass and ProxySet/balancer (parse_status_list now returns statuses plus the unparsable remainder instead of shortening silently). Differential coverage: tests/config_validity.py STRICT_CASES - nine rows where apache2 -t fails, vapached compatible -t loads with the ignore warning, and vapached --strict-config fails (AddType/AddHandler/Header/ExpiresByType/ProxyPass arities, unknown Options and RewriteOptions tokens, ProxyPass and ProxySet failonstatus). Unit test: strict_mode_refuses_silently_dropped_directives in config.rs.

obligations.title: Rewrite rules cannot launder URL policy into an executable target
obligations.evidence: rewrite_scope_retained_admit states that a changed rewrite retains the original URL policy and evaluates the rewritten target; the dispatcher conjoins the original URL's Options/AllowOverride/header policy with the final/rewrite-target scope via restrict_policy_with, while the same-URL target bind performs the full Options+handler meet. Internal URL/file rewrites, terminal proxy/redirect original gates and cache targets use the shared gate; F60 rewrite-laundering and F23/F53/F58 rewrite regressions exercise the shape. The regex/substitution interpreter remains outside Verus; its security consequence is expressed by the verified scope-conjunction and filesystem-containment kernels

obligations.title: Per-directory rewrite URL base, filesystem subject and plan identity
obligations.evidence: request_plan::layer_url_mount is the single URL-mount derivation for access files and main-config <Directory> rewrites; request_plan::layer_subject is the single filesystem-relative RewriteRule subject derivation used by rewrite::subject_for. Every parsed access-file rule carries its layer directory, and htaccess_rewrite_subject_admit requires a derivable subject or fails closed instead of silently skipping a layer. RequestPlan now carries the canonical target, mapping root, relative path, filesystem target and collected access layers for dispatch, cache, rewrite contexts and --explain (I59). Unit plus F53/F58 replays cover prefix Alias, AliasMatch, ScriptAlias, nested .htaccess, explicit RewriteBase, document-root/ancestor layers above the mapping root, and [F]/[G]/[E]/[R] effects

obligations.title: Every non-default handler is dynamic for cache-query isolation
obligations.evidence: cache_dynamic_handler_admit states that a dynamic handler requires a cache bypass; request_scope classifies the effective handler after DirectoryIndex resolution, covering SetHandler proxy:fcgi (direct and index), cgi-script, server-status and future non-default handlers in addition to ProxyPass routes. Unit plus F54 fastcgi-mock replays cover direct and index queries

obligations.title: Cache key material is injective over raw bytes
obligations.evidence: cache_key_hex is refined to cache_key_hex_spec and proved length-preserving and injective (cache_key_hex_spec_injective, hex_byte_spec_injective); base_key hex-encodes server root, host, path, raw query and resolved target bytes, non-UTF-8 URL paths bypass the shared cache, invalid index names are rejected, and invalidation uses the same encoding. Unit plus F55 raw-socket replays cover invalid query bytes versus empty and replacement-byte queries

obligations.title: Local ErrorDocument subrequests are excluded from the original URL cache
obligations.evidence: cache_local_error_document_admit excludes a missing target that can select a local ErrorDocument from lookup/store and refuses to store any response produced by an ErrorDocument internal subrequest (response-provenance marker); existing targets retain normal cache behavior. Unit plus F56 fastcgi-mock replays cover query-dependent local error documents without regressing the Apache cache conformance cases

obligations.title: Only bodyless credential-free GETs with safe response shape enter the cache
obligations.evidence: cache_store_request_admit, cache_store_status_admit, cache_store_control_admit, cache_store_shape_admit and cache_store_ttl_admit mechanize the runtime store gates for method/body/credentials, cacheable statuses, Cache-Control overrides, Set-Cookie/Vary:*/size and positive freshness; cache_ttl_clamp returns zero for reversed CacheMinExpire/CacheMaxExpire instead of panicking. Unit matrix plus conformance cache cases exercise each branch

obligations.title: Location shell-glob compiles at parse time (F61)
obligations.evidence: compile_location_pattern builds MatchKind::LocationGlob/LocationMatch/Location at load time; an unhandleable pattern (a bare `~` with no expression, a malformed regex) is a configuration error and the section is skipped, never an inert literal string. fnmatch_match evaluates the glob with path_mode=true; fnmatch_path_mode_slash_bounded plus the fnmatch_class_end_bounds lemma prove the kernel match stays component-bounded and anchored, and fnmatch_location_glob_oracle pins the 2.4.69 probe verdicts (wildcard covers nested below the prefix, never bridges a sibling prefix, matches the trailing-slash form and not the bare directory). location_wildcard_compiled_admit is debug-asserted at the parse site. F61-A/A2/B/C Python replays cover directive forms and both match-phase placements.

obligations.title: fnmatch class negation honors both markers (F62/F62b)
obligations.evidence: the verified fnmatch kernel treats `[^a]` and `[!a]` identically (fnmatch_class_negated, fnmatch_class_body); fnmatch_class_negation_oracle pins the Apache verdicts for member/non-member basenames in Files globs, Locations and Directory wildcards, and fnmatch_match is the single matcher used by glob_match, Files slots and Location slots (the old hand-rolled matcher and the files_glob_to_regex regex translation are gone, so the `^`-as-literal bug cannot recur). Files-class Python replays and the kernel unit matrix cover negated members, `?` cardinality and basename containment.

obligations.title: expr variables known-set and fail-closed fs vars (F63/F63b)
obligations.evidence: expr_var_known is the single source of truth shared by expr::var evaluation and the load-time validate_vars walker (Expr::Var nodes plus %{...} inside Str with transform-arg recursion). REQUEST_FILENAME/SCRIPT_FILENAME are known only when the context binds fs_path (with_fs_path), so an unbound reference evaluates to Err (fail closed) instead of an empty string; expr_fs_var_bound_admit guards the bound case. Wired at <If>/<ElseIf>, Require expr (unsupported -> fail closed) and RewriteCond expr, in both per-server and per-dir layers. Python replays cover the guard fail-closed and the bound-value forms; the F63b load-time refusal is a config_validity divergence.

obligations.title: SetHandler is a separate precedence field (F64/F64b)
obligations.evidence: SetHandler is parsed into MappingPolicy.set_handler instead of the ordered extension table, so directive order and inheritance cannot reorder it. effective_handler consults the force first (None unforces to the ext table). restrict_with conjoins URL/target forces through set_handler_conjoin_admit with set_handler_conjoin_preserves_force proving a surviving force always comes from one side, and set_handler_precedence_admit is debug-asserted in is_cgi so a force always binds and the ext table can neither remove it nor add execution past it (the attacker .htaccess AddHandler upload chain is dead). [H=...] rewrites write the same field. Python replays cover both directive orders, .htaccess over a SetHandler'ed directory, and the [H] override.

obligations.title: CGI execution needs handler or ScriptAlias plus grant (F65)
obligations.evidence: is_cgi reduces to a single verified kernel call cgi_exec_admit(handler_bound, handler_is_cgi, script_alias, exec_allowed) with cgi_exec_requires_cgi_handler proving no execution without a cgi-script handler bound or a ScriptAlias mapping, and cgi_exec_requires_exec_allowed proving no execution without the Options ExecCGI grant or the alias. A SetHandler default-handler force suppresses a ScriptAlias script; SetHandler None unforces to the ext table. The kernel unit matrix and the F65 replay (source served for a ScriptAlias script under default-handler) pin the behavior.

obligations.title: handler classification uses the lexical basename (F69)
obligations.evidence: the direct dispatch and CGI PATH_INFO split bind classification to the lexical request-mapped basename; FastCGI receives that bound name instead of re-deriving it from SCRIPT_FILENAME. Resolved-target evaluation builds canonical authorization and lexical handler scopes from one immutable RequestPlan/access-layer set, then copies only handlers/set_handler from the lexical Files evaluation. handler_identity_lexical_admit guards classification and handler_scope_lexical_admit proves that a differing resolved target cannot contribute a canonical-only Files/FilesMatch force. Canonical Files authorization remains active. F69 plus five P13 replays cover direct AddHandler, PATH_INFO, FastCGI SetHandler, Files-scoped SetHandler, canonical access denial and live Location controls.

obligations.title: Default-off compatibility surfaces require a process-global capability
obligations.evidence: capability_admit is the executable kernel shared by request parsing, access-file admission and final generated-content/execution sinks; disabled_capability_rejects_request proves a requested surface cannot pass a disabled gate. Main-config compilation records gated effectful directives and validates the final process-global set independent of declaration order; declarations are rejected in vhosts, runtime conditional scopes and access files. Runtime backstops cover TRACE, absolute-form targets, request trailers, autoindex, CGI, FastCGI, the unsafe FastCGI pathname escape hatch and server-status, while program RewriteMap is main-config-only. FastCGI configuration requires an exact stable-path policy or the independent UnstableFastCgiPaths capability, and the final handoff checks that gate again. Audit-loaded configurations are marked non-runnable and refused by dispatch so suppressed reporting diagnostics cannot enable legacy authz or program maps. Unit matrices cover every capability, declaration context/final-state behavior, audit-only loading, final sinks and access-file escalation attempts.
